content:
Halloween 2026 belonged to the impersonators. As the holiday fell on a Saturday, October 31, stars spent the weekend unveiling costumes that were less about monsters and more about each other — family members, pop icons and cartoon favorites, recreated head to toe and posted for the world to judge.

The most talked-about look came from inside one famous family. Kim Kardashian dressed as her own daughter, North West, complete with turquoise-blue hair, faux facial piercings, punk-style jewelry, long charm-studded nails and goth clothing, according to roundups in W Magazine, The Zoe Report and Hello Magazine. The reversal — a mother impersonating her 13-year-old daughter — flipped the usual celebrity-costume formula and dominated costume coverage all weekend.

North West, meanwhile, had her own viral moment, transforming into reality star Natalie Nunn with a prosthetic chin, an angled bob and a "Baddies" necklace. In a twist that completed the triangle, Nunn then dressed as North West herself, posting in turquoise pigtails and a studded collar.

Paris Hilton, twice over

Paris Hilton kept up her Halloween tradition with not one but two headline looks. For her Britney Spears tribute — her fourth Halloween in a row honoring the pop star — Hilton recreated Spears' 2001 MTV Video Music Awards performance of "I'm a Slave 4 U," python included. She also dressed as Belle from Beauty and the Beast, with her toddlers Phoenix and London as Chip and Lumière.

Elsewhere, the nostalgia ran deep. Camila Mendes and Madelaine Petsch paired up as Betty Rubble and Wilma Flintstone, while Keke Palmer and her son Leodis recreated the black-and-white style of Michael and Janet Jackson's "Scream" video. Lizzo drew attention as Seiko Ayase from the anime series Dandadan, and Lisa Rinna dressed as Kylie Jenner in an orange Chrome Hearts outfit.

Harry Styles revisited his own past, nodding to his teenage X Factor audition look and to Elvis Presley, while Zendaya recreated an iconic Halle Berry look and Janelle Monáe returned with her annual Wondaween celebration. Owen Thiele and Benito Skinner paired up as PinkPantheress and Zara Larsson, recreating one of the year's buzziest pop collaborations.

Analysis: Why impersonation won Halloween

What stands out about Halloween 2026 is how little explanation any of these costumes needed. A viewer recognizes North West's blue hair, Britney's 2001 python moment or the Flintstones' palette instantly — and that instant recognition is the point. In a social-media holiday, the costume is no longer just something worn to a party; it is a piece of content engineered to travel, and familiarity is what makes it travel.

There is also a branding logic at work. Kardashian doubling down on her daughter's much-discussed edgy look reads as a public show of support, while Hilton's annual Spears tribute has become its own tradition, as reliable as the holiday itself. The stars who won the weekend were not the ones in the scariest masks — they were the ones who understood that, in 2026, the best costume is a reference everyone already shares.
